 Netflix has hired Roberto Stanichi, a nearly 20-year veteran of Mattel , to be VP of Consumer Products and Experiences as the streaming giant looks to boost its off-screen presence.
 Mattel just announced the exec’s exit as part of its third-quarter earnings report, noting that it has promoted Steve Totzke to the role of President and Chief Operating Officer. The toy maker, which has explored Hollywood in recent years with Barbie and other projects, is going through a leadership transition. Former CEO Ynon Kreiz departed several weeks ago to become Co-CEO of Skydance, with board member and tech and media vet Roger Lynch then installed as chief exec.

 At Mattel, Stanichi most recently held the title of President and Chief Marketing and Brand Officer. At Netflix, he will oversee Netflix’s global consumer products licensing and retail business, along with global experiences, including Netflix House . He will report to CMO Marian Lee.
 Watch on Deadline 
 “Roberto has spent his career turning iconic characters and stories into global brands that resonate across generations,” Lee said. “As we continue to build on the incredible fandom around Netflix’s stories and characters, his experience will be invaluable in shaping how those connections extend beyond the screen and into fans’ everyday lives.”
 In his two-decade run at Mattel, Stanichi led the company’s global brand organization across Barbie, Hot Wheels, Fisher-Price, and American Girl. He managed a number of entertainment titles as they made a strong showing in consumer products. Stanichi also expanded the adult fan base across multiple brands, and teamed with Disney to establish Disney Pixar Cars as an evergreen brand. Additionally, he also played a key role in the co-master toy partnership between Mattel and Hasbro for Netflix’s KPop Demon Hunters , which was an industry first.
 Compared with media rivals like Disney, Comcast and Skydance, Netflix’s consumer products business is in an early phase of development, but it has been ramping up around major tentpoles in recent years. Stranger Things provided the initial foundation for the consumer products effort, with a line of Funko Pop figures accompanying the show’s first season. By the fifth and final season in 2025, the series anchored the company’s largest global licensing program to date.
 Bridgerton and Kpop also drove considerable interest across consumer products, with the sequel to the latter due to get an amplified push from a full theatrical release. The first film screened in movie theaters months after being embraced by streaming audiences.
 On the experiences front, Netflix has launched more than 50 separate formats bridging film and TV titles and the real world. The company says it has reached 15 million fans across 490 openings in more than 300 cities around the world.
 In fall 2025, Netflix launched Netflix House, a destination for games and interactive and immersive experiences related to multiple properties. There are Netflix Houses in the Philadelphia and Dallas markets, with a third location set to open next year on the Las Vegas Strip.
 “Few companies in the world understand the emotional power of storytelling and fandom like Netflix,” Stanichi said in a statement. “It is an incredible privilege to join Marian and this extraordinary team to help expand that fandom into physical worlds, products, and experiences. Netflix’s culture of bold innovation and creative ambition is legendary, and I’m excited to dive in to create impactful touchpoints that bring our fans closer to the stories they love.”
